title: Bounds on the Expansion Properties of Tanner Graphs
evidence: Primary text and hypotheses inspected; source questions screened with hashes and locators in literature/stopping-bound-source-screening.json
limit: The bit-oriented bound is s(H) >= n(2γ−η)/(γk−η), η=σ₂², with binary regular incidence. It concerns the same graph stopping distance, but does not construct QC-GHP matrices meeting η<γ/2. The parity-oriented bound and multi-eigenvector expansion analysis supply older alternatives to the weak mixing step.

title: Minimum Distance Bounds by Graph Analysis
evidence: Primary text and hypotheses inspected; source questions screened with hashes and locators in literature/stopping-bound-source-screening.json
limit: Theorems assume a connected regular bipartite graph, with constant bit and check degrees. Theorem 3.1 gives n(2γ−η)/(γk−η) for classical distance. Its at-least-two-active-bits proof is the ancestor of Zhu–Chugg’s explicit stopping-distance extension. This is not the same γ/2 test, nor a QC-GHP parameter theorem. The manuscript reports an earlier 1982 submission; this is not treated as an inspected 1982 publication.

title: Quantum Tanner codes
evidence: Primary text and hypotheses inspected; source questions screened with hashes and locators in literature/stopping-bound-source-screening.json
limit: Ramanujan expansion is imposed on constituent Cayley graphs, together with local-code distance, dual-tensor robustness, puncturing resistance and total no-conjugacy. It is not a statement that the expanded CSS parity-check matrix has σ₂²<γ/2. It does not furnish parameters for Proposition 5.1. Efficient decoding is a historical question in this 2022 version; current resolution is deliberately unassessed in this screen.
